items.headline: Man, 30, charged with nine offences over fatal Tampines Avenue 12 hit-and-run
items.summary: A married couple, both 24, died after a crash involving two cars and a motorcycle on Tampines Avenue 12 on the night of Oct 29; the wife was a month pregnant and they leave a six-year-old son. A 30-year-old man arrested on Oct 30 was charged on Oct 31 with nine offences including dangerous driving causing death, having allegedly fled the scene and driven a deregistered car with a cloned plate while disqualified.

items.headline: HDB to redevelop Toa Payoh West with more than 6,000 new homes
items.summary: HDB announced a decade-long redevelopment of Toa Payoh West, adding more than 6,000 mostly public-housing units, a new shopping mall near Caldecott MRT and a 1.2-hectare wellness park. From the November 2026 sales exercise, the eligibility age for community care apartments will be lowered from 65 to 55.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines and Scoot put more than 380,000 discounted tickets on sale
items.summary: Singapore Airlines and its budget arm Scoot released over 380,000 promotional fares across economy, premium economy and business class in a sale running Oct 23 to 30, covering routes in Asia, Europe and beyond.

items.headline: Delivery rider blind in one eye loses bid for monthly maintenance from ex-wife
items.summary: A 51-year-old food-delivery rider in Singapore, blind in one eye and with a serious heart condition, failed to secure S$500 in monthly maintenance from his ex-wife after a court found his earnings exceeded his stated living costs.

items.headline: ISRO's GSLV-F18 launches NVS-03, restoring the NavIC navigation system
items.summary: ISRO placed the NVS-03 navigation satellite in orbit aboard GSLV-F18 on Oct 31, its second GSLV flight in two months, bringing the indigenous NavIC regional navigation constellation back to operational strength.

items.headline: Helicopter returning from Badrinath crashes near Joshimath, killing all six aboard
items.summary: A helicopter carrying five pilgrims and a pilot from Badrinath toward Dehradun crashed near Joshimath in Uttarakhand around 2pm on Oct 31, killing everyone on board; five of the dead were from Karnataka.

items.headline: Supreme Court says intimacy in a soured relationship is not automatically rape
items.summary: The Supreme Court quashed a rape case, holding that consensual physical intimacy does not become rape merely because a relationship later broke down, noting the complainant had been told of the man's existing marriage within months of their living together.

items.headline: Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi says he will quit the National Conference
items.summary: Srinagar Lok Sabha MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi announced he will leave the National Conference, saying the party's problems could not be fixed from within, in a public break with the Omar Abdullah-led party.

items.headline: RJD's Anil Jha wins a Bihar MLC seat on second preferences after trailing all 10 rounds
items.summary: In the Darbhanga graduate-constituency MLC election, RJD's Anil Kumar Jha beat the BJP's Sarvesh Kumar by 450 votes on second-preference counting, despite trailing through all 10 rounds of first-preference votes.

items.headline: UK gilt yields fall to a five-week low as Burnham's budget wins back bond investors
items.summary: UK government bonds rallied after Prime Minister Andy Burnham's first budget, with the 10-year gilt yield dropping to around 5.25% on Oct 29 and heading for its biggest monthly fall since May, as investors welcomed a dose of fiscal restraint.

items.headline: UK house prices stall in October as mortgage costs bite, Nationwide says
items.summary: Average UK house prices were broadly unchanged in October at £273,566, Nationwide reported, after a 0.3% fall in September and against economists' expectations of a 0.2% drop, as high borrowing costs continue to weigh on demand.

items.headline: Burnham says the UK budget was not what he would want in an 'ideal world'
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham distanced himself from his own government's first budget, saying its room for manoeuvre 'wasn't what I would have hoped', after Chancellor John Healey leaned on dozens of smaller measures rather than big tax-and-spend moves.

items.headline: UK debt office tilts gilt sales toward shorter maturities amid market volatility
items.summary: The UK Debt Management Office revised its gilt-issuance plan, pulling back from long-dated bonds and shifting toward shorter maturities that are less exposed to market swings, after investor demand changed following the budget.

items.headline: Thousands rally in Berlin as Gen Z protests spread across more than 30 German cities
items.summary: A youth movement calling itself 'Gen Z Regelt' staged protests in Berlin and more than 30 German cities on Oct 31 over the cost of living, underfunded schools and a possible return of conscription; organisers said tens of thousands registered, while Berlin police counted about 5,000.

items.headline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo passes 5,000 in the country's deadliest outbreak on record
items.summary: Government data showed more than 5,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak, out of over 10,000 infections since May. It is the country's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record, and there is still no approved vaccine or treatment.

items.headline: Iran calls US outreach a 'positive step' as a delegation holds talks in Qatar
items.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described US efforts to open dialogue as 'a positive step' on Oct 31 but ruled out meeting US officials for now, as an Iranian delegation in Doha reviewed Qatari-mediated proposals.

items.headline: G20 scraps its group photo in Atlanta as European ministers refuse to stand with Lavrov
items.summary: The traditional group photo at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta was cancelled after European ministers objected to Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov's presence; the meeting ended Oct 30 with no joint communique, and the US said it would issue a chair's statement.

items.headline: Al Jazeera investigation maps Sudanese commanders linked to wartime sexual violence
items.summary: An Al Jazeera investigation published Oct 30 identified commanders in Sudan's Rapid Support Forces tied to sexual violence during the war, days after the UK sanctioned 15 senior figures from Sudan's rival forces over suspected atrocities.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts its funding target by $10 billion to about $20 billion as AI stocks slide
items.summary: OpenAI has lowered its latest fundraising target to roughly $20 billion from $30 billion and trimmed its valuation goal to about $1.25 trillion from $1.4 trillion, with an AI-stock selloff and rival Anthropic's impending IPO weighing on investor appetite, the Financial Times reported.

items.headline: South Korea's FuriosaAI raises $620 million, quadrupling its valuation to $2.9 billion
items.summary: Seoul-based AI chip startup FuriosaAI closed a $620 million round that lifted its valuation to $2.9 billion, with South Korea's National Growth Fund contributing $280 million, as it builds inference chips to challenge Nvidia after rejecting an $800 million Meta takeover.

items.headline: Ex-Palantir engineers launch Dream with $17 million to build AI 'world models' for construction
items.summary: Startup Dream emerged from stealth with a $17 million seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz to build AI world models that automate building design and engineering, and says it is already deployed on 10 active projects in Texas and California.

items.headline: US Justice Department scrutinises Nvidia's roughly $13 billion Hugging Face deal
items.summary: The Justice Department is asking how Nvidia's roughly $13 billion acquisition of AI platform Hugging Face, announced in September, would affect competition in the AI market, according to a Reuters report; no formal challenge has been filed and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: Big Tech's AI capital spending diverges as nerves over the boom grow
items.summary: A review of the week's earnings showed Microsoft cloud revenue of $63.9 billion but capital spending of $45.2 billion, below its own plan, while Meta raised its 2026 capex floor to $135-145 billion and posted negative free cash flow, feeding investor unease even as AI demand holds up.

items.headline: Bank of Japan holds its policy rate at 1.25%, its highest since 1995
items.summary: The Bank of Japan kept its benchmark rate at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote on Oct 30, with Hajime Takata dissenting for an immediate hike, and said underlying inflation is now broadly consistent with its 2% target for the first time since 2013; economists expect a further hike by January.

items.headline: Euro-zone growth slows to 0.4% in the third quarter as France unexpectedly contracts
items.summary: Eurostat's flash estimate put euro-zone GDP growth at 0.4% in the third quarter, above the 0.2% expected but down from 0.6%; France shrank 0.1%, Germany grew 0.2%, Italy stagnated and Spain expanded 0.6%.

items.headline: US economy grows 3.4% in the third quarter as September inflation accelerates
items.summary: US GDP rose at a 3.4% annualised rate in the third quarter, above the 3.1% expected and up from 2.2%, while the Fed's preferred PCE gauge climbed 0.5% in September to a 3.6% annual rate; the Federal Reserve had held rates at 3.75-4% days earlier.

items.headline: Merck beats third-quarter estimates and raises its full-year profit outlook
items.summary: Merck posted adjusted earnings of $2.49 a share on revenue of $18.09 billion, both above expectations, helped by Keytruda including its new injectable form, and lifted its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $2.77-$2.82.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen and Lawson hit with grid penalties for 'unacceptable' Mexico practice clash
items.summary: Formula 1 stewards gave Max Verstappen and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson a one-place grid drop and a superlicence penalty point each for their collision in second practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, meaning Verstappen cannot start Sunday's race from pole whatever he does in qualifying.

items.headline: 🏎️ Norris edges title leader Antonelli by 0.001s in final Mexico practice
items.summary: Lando Norris topped final practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix with a 1:17.600, just 0.001s ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen fifth, setting up a tight qualifying fight.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz beats Medvedev to reach the Vienna final against De Minaur
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Daniil Medvedev 6-4, 7-6(2) in the Vienna semifinals to reach his fifth tour-level final of 2026, where he will meet Alex de Minaur, who came through the other semifinal.

items.headline: 🎾 Vacherot upsets Fritz to reach the Basel final
items.summary: Valentin Vacherot beat sixth seed Taylor Fritz 7-6(5), 6-3 to become the first player from Monaco to reach the Swiss Indoors Basel final, where he will face Jiri Lehecka, who saved a match point to beat Jan-Lennard Struff 3-6, 7-5, 6-4.

items.headline: 🏏 New Zealand thrash India by 87 runs as Phillips smashes a 49-ball century
items.summary: Glenn Phillips hit 107 off 49 balls and Jacob Duffy took 4-23 as New Zealand made 259-7 and bowled India out for 172 in the fourth T20I at Eden Park; India still lead the five-match series 3-1.

items.headline: 🏏 South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs to take the series 2-1 as Harmer claims 10 wickets
items.summary: Simon Harmer took match figures of 10 wickets, including 6-16, as Australia were bowled out for 111 chasing 288 on day five of the Cape Town Test; South Africa won the three-match series 2-1 and knocked Australia off the top of the Test rankings.

items.headline: Spacewalking astronauts install the final roll-out solar array on the ISS
items.summary: NASA's Anil Menon and Canada's Joshua Kutryk spent 7 hours 11 minutes outside the International Space Station on Oct 29 to install and deploy its seventh roll-out solar array; a final array follows on Nov 5, together lifting station power by up to 30%.

items.headline: Hubble and Webb capture the ghostly Cat's Head Nebula in new images
items.summary: NASA released a joint Hubble and James Webb view of the Cat's Head Nebula, a dusty star-forming region within the Carina Nebula roughly 7,500 light-years away, pairing visible-light and infrared images to reveal its glowing dust filaments.

items.headline: Study finds 'charismatic' fossils like dinosaurs dominate top science journals
items.summary: An analysis of thousands of palaeontology papers by Bryan Gee of Seattle's Burke Museum found that dinosaurs, mammals and other glamorous species are over-represented in Nature and Science relative to other taxonomic groups, reigniting debate over publication bias.

items.headline: Flickering brain signals in monkeys may hold a clue to consciousness
items.summary: Researchers led by Doris Tsao at the University of California, Berkeley reported that macaques' brain activity flips about 15 times a second between patterns tied to images they consciously see and images outside their awareness, letting the team reconstruct both from neural data alone, in work reported by Nature.

fun_fact.headline: Koala fingerprints resemble human fingerprints
fun_fact.body: Koalas have fingerprints so similar to a human's that even under a microscope they can be hard to tell apart. The looping, whorled ridges evolved independently from ours — close relatives like wombats and kangaroos lack them — most likely to help the animals grip and handle eucalyptus leaves.
fun_fact.source: PBS NOVA; University of Adelaide (Henneberg) research

puzzle.title: Fair Exchange
puzzle.body:
A trader sells two watches for $120 each. On the first he makes a 20% profit; on the second he takes a 20% loss.
Overall, does he come out ahead, behind, or exactly even — and by how much?
puzzle.approach: Work out the actual cost price hidden behind each sale price before you compare them.
puzzle.answer:
He loses $10.
The first watch cost $120 ÷ 1.20 = $100 and sold for $120, a $20 gain.
The second cost $120 ÷ 0.80 = $150 and sold for $120, a $30 loss.
Total cost $250 against total revenue $240 — so he is $10 (about 4%) worse off, even though the two 20% figures look like they should cancel.

word_puzzle.title: Count on It
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange all the letters of the phrase

ELEVEN PLUS TWO

to form a different three-word phrase. Remarkably, the new phrase has the same numerical value as the original. What is it?
word_puzzle.approach: Rearrange every letter of the phrase; the answer is just another way of writing the same number.
word_puzzle.answer:
TWELVE PLUS ONE.
It uses exactly the same thirteen letters as ELEVEN PLUS TWO — three E's, two L's, and one each of N, O, P, S, T, U, V and W.
And, fittingly, both phrases equal 13.
